content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 is involved in the metabolism of many drugs. Danicopan increases the plasma levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. Danicopan also increases the plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates, necessitating dose adjustments of these substrates as per their prescribing information. 2. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 3. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 4. Deferasirox decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Deferasirox also decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. 5. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of deferiprone by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, zinc), so administration should be separated by at least 4 hours from antacids or supplements containing these cations. 6. Deferoxamine decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Deferoxamine chelates iron, which may impact iron supplementation. 7. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Oral delafloxacin forms chelate with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 8. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) such as desipramine, dosulepin, and doxepin, leading to increased serum concentrations and a higher risk of adverse effects. The clinical significance of these interactions is minor or unknown, but monitoring is advised. 10. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 13. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. 14. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by weakly inducing CYP3A4. Nonhormonal contraceptives or barrier methods should be used during elafibranor treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 15. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by weak-to-moderate induction of CYP3A4. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended during treatment and for 1 week after discontinuation. 16. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Ferrous fumarate decreases eltrombopag levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. 18. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Fezolinetant is contraindicated with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 20. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of fleroxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Felbamate decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 24. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of exemestane by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use with estrogen-containing products. 26. Ethinylestradiol may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Exenatide may reduce the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 27. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Erythromycin derivatives (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods. 31. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended.
